facts.claim: The effects of income inequality on social and institutional trust were systematically nonsignificant and smaller than the smallest negative effect of interest.
facts.quote: Second, the effects of income inequality on social and institutional trust were systematically nonsignificant and smaller than the smallest negative effect of interest.

facts.claim: The effects of social class on social trust were systematically positive.
facts.quote: First, the effects of social class on social trust were systematically positive, whereas the effects on institutional trust depended on the way social class was measured.

facts.claim: The negative link between income inequality and the happiness of lower-income respondents was explained not by lower household income, but by perceived unfairness and lack of trust.
facts.quote: Most important, we found that the negative link between income inequality and the happiness of lower-income respondents was explained not by lower household income, but by perceived unfairness and lack of trust.

facts.claim: Americans trusted other people less in years with more national income inequality than in years with less national income inequality.
facts.quote: Americans trusted other people less and perceived other people to be less fair in the years with more national income inequality than in the years with less national income inequality.

facts.claim: Lack of trust is more common in more unequal societies.
facts.quote: Recent evidence suggests that many other social problems, including mental illness, violence, imprisonment, lack of trust, teenage births, obesity, drug abuse, and poor educational performance of schoolchildren, are also more common in more unequal societies.

research.angle: While some studies link income inequality to lower trust, a large-scale analysis suggests that social class—not income inequality—is the actual predictor of social trust.
research.verdict: The evidence is contradictory, as one study finds income inequality linked to lower trust while a larger study finds the effect of income inequality on trust to be nonsignificant.
research.caveat: The findings are limited by inconsistencies in how social class is measured and the small number of higher-level units available in some research.
